title: Can Carpet Be Installed Over Existing Carpet, Hardwood or Concrete?
meta: Carpet over old carpet is a no, over hardwood needs care, over concrete is routine. Wills Flooring installs carpet in Seattle from $0.99 per sq ft, labor.
keywords: can you install carpet over carpet, carpet over hardwood floors, carpet over concrete basement, installing carpet on concrete slab, carpet over existing carpet padding, tack strip on hardwood

blocks.lead: Carpet should never go over existing carpet, it can go over hardwood if you accept tack strip holes, and it goes over concrete all the time once the slab passes a moisture test.
blocks.detail: The rule is simple: new carpet needs a firm, clean, dry base and something to stretch against. Old carpet fails that test, hardwood raises a should-you question, and concrete just needs the right pad and fasteners. Stretch-in labor is $0.99 per sq ft, glue-down over a slab is $1.29, and pulling the old carpet and pad adds $0.45.

blocks.html: This comes up in three very different Seattle houses. A Beacon Hill landlord wants new carpet over the tired carpet in a rental to skip a tear-out. A Wallingford buyer just found oak under the bedroom carpet and wants soft floors anyway. A Capitol Hill condo owner or a West Seattle basement has a bare slab and a plan. Each has its own honest answer.

blocks.text: Carpet over existing carpet: why every installer says no

items.title: Pad on pad means no stretch
items.text: Stretch-in carpet is pulled tight over a dense pad and hooked onto tack strip at the walls. Old carpet is soft and moves under the new one, so the new carpet never holds tension. Within months it ripples, and the wrinkles walk across the room.

items.title: You seal in 15 years of what is in there
items.text: Old carpet holds dust, dander, spills and, in a lot of Seattle rentals, cat urine that reached the pad. Covering it does not remove the smell, it traps it under a layer that cannot be cleaned. Allergies get worse, not better.

items.title: Doors and transitions stop working
items.text: Two layers of carpet and pad add well over an inch. Doors drag, the tile threshold becomes a trip edge, and closet doors on tracks stop closing. In a 1920s Ballard house with original doors, planing them is not something you want to do.

items.title: No warranty covers it
items.text: Every manufacturer requires new carpet over an approved pad on a clean subfloor. Go over old carpet and the material warranty is void on day one, and no installer will warranty the stretch. The tear-out you skipped comes back as a replacement.

blocks.text: Carpet over hardwood: it works, but ask yourself why

blocks.html: Mechanically, hardwood is a great base for carpet: flat, firm, dry, and tack strip nails into it easily. The problem is the other direction. Half the hardwood floors we refinish in Seattle came out from under carpet, and the tack strip holes along every wall are the tell. If the wood under your carpet is oak or old-growth fir in decent shape, refinishing is often the better long-term move. If you still want carpet, here is how to do it without ruining the wood.

blocks.text: Carpet over concrete: routine, with three conditions

items.text: Seattle slabs in daylight basements and on-grade condos are cool and often damp. A calcium chloride or relative humidity test tells us whether the slab can take carpet and what pad it needs.
items.note: A slab that fails is not a dead end; it changes the pad and sometimes the carpet type.

items.text: Over a slab we use a pad with a moisture barrier film or a synthetic fiber pad that does not absorb water. Standard rebond soaks up slab moisture and starts to smell within a couple of winters.
Wood-floor tack strip has short pins. Concrete strip has hardened masonry nails, or it is glued where the slab is too hard or has heat tubes. Either way the carpet stretches the same.

A slab in a West Seattle basement sits near ground temperature all year. A thicker, denser pad makes a real difference in comfort and is the main reason people carpet down there instead of using vinyl plank.

blocks.text: When concrete is the wrong base for carpet

items.html: The slab has flooded or wicks water in winter. Seattle basements dug into a hillside with no working drain are a recurring theme. Fix the water first; no pad survives a wet slab.
Efflorescence or dark patches that never dry. White mineral bloom means water is moving through the slab. That room wants vinyl plank, not carpet.
Radiant heat in the slab. Carpet over heated concrete works, but only with a thin, low insulation pad, and you cannot nail tack strip into a slab with tubes in it. We glue the strip instead.

blocks.text: What to have ready before we come out

items: Pull back a corner of the old carpet in a closet and look. Wood, plywood, particleboard or concrete each change the plan.
In a condo, get the building's flooring rules. Many Seattle buildings specify a sound rating for pad and set quiet hours.
Tell us about smells or past leaks. We would rather see a stain on the subfloor than seal it under new carpet.
Know your priority: warmth, quiet, allergies or resale. It decides carpet versus refinish over hardwood.

faq.q: Can you lay new carpet on top of old carpet to save money?
faq.a: No. New carpet needs a firm base to stretch against, and old carpet is soft and moves. The new carpet ripples within months, doors stop clearing, trapped odors stay trapped, and both warranties are void. Tear-out is only $0.45 per sq ft including haul-away, so the saving is never worth it.

faq.q: Does carpet ruin hardwood floors underneath?
faq.a: Not the carpet itself. The damage is tack strip nail holes around the perimeter and pad staples in the field, both of which sand out at a future refinish. Water from steam cleaning is the real risk, especially on old-growth fir in older Seattle homes. Keep cleaning dry and the wood is fine.

faq.q: Should I carpet over the hardwood or refinish it?
faq.a: If the wood is oak or fir with sanding thickness left and the room is a living area, refinishing usually adds more value in Seattle. Carpet over hardwood makes sense in bedrooms, in condos with sound requirements, and in homes where warmth and quiet matter more than resale.

faq.q: Do you need a special pad for carpet over concrete?
faq.a: Yes. Over a slab we use a pad with a moisture barrier film or a non-absorbent synthetic fiber pad. Standard rebond wicks moisture from cool Seattle slabs and develops a musty smell. We moisture test the slab first so the pad choice matches conditions in your basement or condo.

faq.q: How is tack strip attached to concrete?
faq.a: Concrete tack strip uses hardened masonry nails driven into the slab, or it is glued with construction adhesive when the slab is very hard, crumbly, or has radiant tubing in it. Once the strip is down, the carpet is power stretched onto it just as it would be on wood.

faq.q: Can carpet go over a concrete basement floor that has had water before?
faq.a: Only after the water problem is solved and the slab tests dry. A basement that seeps every winter will ruin any pad and grow mold under the carpet. Fix the drainage or sealing first, retest, and if the slab still reads damp, vinyl plank is the safer floor down there.
